typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

facility.description: The Facility associated with the WorkOrder

statusCode.description:
The status code for the WorkOrder
Customer-specific codes indicating current status of the work order, e.g. Assigned to field

workOrderNumber.description:
The WorkOrder number specified
A customer-specific identifier for the work order. Not used internally as a key

workOrderType.description:
The type of the WorkOrder
The highest-level classification for a work order, e.g. customer requested in region X.

workSubtype.description:
The work subtype of the WorkOrder
A finer distinction within a workType
e.g. work type might indicate a reconnect of power
work sub type might indicate because the customer has paid their back bill
or indicate that a new customer has moved in

workType.description:
The work type of the WorkOrder, is a property on the parentWorkOrder
The type of work order, describes the actual work that must be done for the work order
e.g. reconnection of power

workStartDate.description: The work start date of the WorkOrder

workEndDate.description:
The work end date of the WorkOrder
The more important of the two dates in most metrics as it indicates when to start looking for aberrant behavior

openedDate.description: The opened date for the WorkOrder

comments.description: Allows back office or field investigators to provide other important information about the work order

resolution.description:
The resolution of the WorkOrder
e.g. "Completed Job" or "Confirmed - Unable to bill"

resolutionTime.description:
The time it took to resolve the WorkOrder
specified by ExactDimension with value and unit of measurement

timestamp.description:
The timestamp on the WorkOrder
Usually used to indicate when the work order was created
while workStartDate and workEndDate indicate the actual work time span

serviceGroup.description: The service group responsible for the WorkOrder

serviceTeam.description: The service team within the service group responsible for the WorkOrder

technician.description: The technician associated with the WorkOrder

asset.description: The asset associated with the WorkOrder

customer.description: The customer associated with the WorkOrder

location.description: The location associated with the WorkOrder

customerOrg.description: The organization associated with the WorkOrder

parentWorkOrder.description: The original WorkOrder created, this could have subtasks such as child WorkOrders or WorkItems

childWorkOrders.description:
Separate work orders spawned from the original WorkOrder.
In Enel, for a while we stored WorkItems in WorkOrder and used childWorkOrders to link them,
but that was confusing and made the WorkOrder table too large to be performant.

workItems.description:
The work items for the WorkOrder
specific sub-tasks that are associated with the work order.

reasonCode.description: The internal code that corresponds with the reason for the work order

title: WorkOrders are requests to perform work on any part of the grid.
name: WorkOrder
